correctness.rationale: The stationary Poisson stochastic convolution has an all-real mgf: Dt²/(2k)+r/(2k)*integral_0^(sigma² t²/2)(e^v-1)dv/v. Choosing t=sqrt(2)(1-epsilon)sqrt(log x)/sigma makes mgf subleading relative to t*x, giving Chernoff liminf >=sqrt(2)/sigma. A burst of about (1+epsilon)x/(sigma sqrt(2log x)) kicks during last 1/log x, with each Gaussian mark near sigma sqrt(2 log x), costs n*(2 log x+o(log x)); independent older bath is nonnegative with probability at least half. This gives matching limsup and symmetry handles other tails. Independently confirmed exact second and fourth stationary cumulant coefficients and sampled large-log event costs; finite diagnostics do not establish limit.
